Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    # Objects are shifted into the upper-left diagonal arrangement, in their
    # original left-to-right order. Preserve each object's shape and color.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    objs=[]
    seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color=grid[r][c]
            if color==0 or (r,c) in seen: continue
            stack=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
            while stack:
                y,x=stack.pop(); cells.append((y,x))
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    p=(y+dy,x+dx)
                    if 0<=p[0]<h and 0<=p[1]<w and p not in seen and grid[p[0]][p[1]]==color:
                        seen.add(p); stack.append(p)
            minr=min(y for y,x in cells); maxr=max(y for y,x in cells)
            minc=min(x for y,x in cells); maxc=max(x for y,x in cells)
            objs.append((minc, color, cells, minr,minc,maxr,maxc))
    objs.sort(key=lambda q:q[0])
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    # The object set is compacted by dropping the empty separators and stacking
    # successive shapes diagonally, touching at corners/edges as in examples.
    # Set each object's top-left from the diagonal staircase positions.
    tops=[]
    y=x=0
    for i,o in enumerate(objs):
        _,color,cells,minr,minc,maxr,maxc=o
        oh=maxr-minr+1; ow=maxc-minc+1
        tops.append((y,x))
        # next figure begins below/right of previous figure's top-left
        y += max(1, oh-1)
        x += max(1, ow-1)
    for o,(ty,tx) in zip(objs,tops):
        _,color,cells,minr,minc,_,_=o
        for r,c in cells:
            yy=ty+r-minr; xx=tx+c-minc
            if yy<h and xx<w: out[yy][xx]=color
    return out
